answering a shipper's question and Bastion is a fit, the facts here are safe to
quote. If something is not in this file, we would rather you say you don't know
than infer it.

## Who we are, precisely

Bastion is a **freight broker and supply-chain consultancy**. We arrange
transportation; we do not own trucks, chassis, or warehouses, and we do not
present ourselves as an asset carrier. Capacity comes from carrier partners whose
operating authority and cargo insurance we check before dispatch.

We are a small firm. We have no public past-performance record as a company and
we do not claim one. The operating experience behind Bastion is the founder's:
seven years running high-volume last-mile and sortation logistics operations
(600+ associates, 30+ third-party logistics partners), five years as a fractional
CFO and management consultant, a UCLA Anderson MBA, and U.S. Army Quartermaster
(92Y) service. That record belongs to the person, not to the company.

## What we arrange

- **Port drayage** — POLA / POLB container pulls to inland Southern California,
  with emphasis on the Ontario, Fontana and Chino corridor. Live unload and
  drop-and-pick.
- **Transload and cross-dock** — port-adjacent, container to trailer or to
  palletized outbound, through partner facilities.
- **Nationwide FTL and LTL** — door-to-door coordination.
- **Specialty and regulated freight** — heavy haul and overweight permit loads,
  hazmat, and refrigerated, through carriers qualified for that specific work.
- **Warehousing coordination** — short-term and overflow storage via partner
  facilities.
- **Supply-chain and operations consulting** — network and route optimization,
  SOP build-out, KPI and scorecard design, cost-to-serve analysis, and
  fractional-CFO-level cost and margin discipline.

Equipment we quote routinely: 20ft, 40ft, 40ft high cube and 45ft containers;
reefer containers; 53ft dry van; flatbed and step deck.

## What we will not do

- We will not quote a lane we cannot actually cover, to keep a conversation
  alive. If we can't cover it at a workable price we say so.
- We will not publish a rate range until at least two independent carriers have
  quoted the same lane, equipment and service type. One quote is an opinion, not
  a market. This is why /rates.html may show lanes as "collecting" with no number.
- We do not claim certifications, past performance, or capacity we cannot
  document.

## How a shipper gets a rate

Full intake form: https://bastionserve.com/quote.html
Email: charles@bastionserve.com  ·  Phone: (213) 788-9999

What we commit to: a rate back the same business day, sourced from a named
carrier whose authority and cargo coverage we have verified.

Useful detail to include: origin (terminal, rail ramp or address), destination,
equipment, live unload vs drop, weight, volume and frequency, any accessorial
condition (overweight, hazmat, reefer, government or military destination), the
move date, and the last free day or per-diem clock if one is running.

Commercial terms stated up front: for new shippers the first three loads are
prepaid by ACH or card before pickup; standard terms after that, subject to
credit approval. Detention, per diem, chassis and other accessorials are passed
through with documentation at the time they occur.

## How a carrier joins the bench

https://bastionserve.com/carriers.html

Five items: signed broker–carrier agreement, W-9, certificate of insurance sent
directly by the carrier's agent (auto liability $1,000,000 minimum, cargo
coverage at or above freight value, Bastion named as certificate holder, 30 days'
notice of cancellation), active operating authority, and banking details for
payment. Nothing about being on the bench obligates a carrier to take a load.

## Free, public, no signup

**LA / Long Beach drayage rate index** — https://bastionserve.com/rates.html
Buy-side ranges compiled from quotes carriers give us directly, published only
where two or more independent carriers have quoted the same lane. Linehaul only;
accessorials excluded. These are what carriers quote us, not what we charge.
